item.title: Videos show explosions across Caracas, Venezuela
item.description: Aircraft, explosions, and smoke were seen across Caracas, the capital of Venezuela, from about 2 a.m.

item.title: The most important things Trump said about the operation that captured Venezuela's Nicolás Maduro
item.description: In the aftermath of the attack on Venezuela, the president said the US would be running the country and bringing in American oil companies.

item.title: Satellite images taken before and after US strikes show damage at a key Venezuelan military site
item.description: New imagery obtained by Business Insider shows widespread damage at a military complex in the southern part of Caracas.

item.title: I stopped being the first to reach out to friends. It made me realize I don't need to be liked by everyone.
item.description: Pulling back from friendships showed me exactly who wanted me in their lives — and it finally quieted my lifelong fear of rejection.

item.title: Venezuela updates: Flights over the Caribbean are set to resume at 12 am ET
item.description: The US captured Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife in a military operation Saturday. They face drugs and weapons charges in New York.

item.title: VIDEO: US Military Captures Venezuelan President In Dramatic Raid
item.description: The US military captured Venezuelan president Nicolas Maduro and his wife during a dramatic raid in Caracas.

item.title: My family is stranded in Puerto Rico because our flights were canceled. It's having an impact on our finances.
item.description: A mother describes how her family was stranded in Puerto Rico after flight cancellations following the capture of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro.

item.title: A group of about 20 US investors is already planning a trip to Venezuela in March
item.description: Charles Myers, chairman of Signum Global Advisors, told Business Insider he is preparing a group of 15-20 investors to travel to Venezuela in March.

item.title: Thousands of travelers stranded as US strikes on Venezuela push airlines out of Caribbean airspace
item.description: From outbound vacationers to students returning for the new semester, the US raid on Venezuela disrupted travel across the region.

item.title: Here's what the smartest people in foreign policy, business, and economics are saying about Trump's raid on Venezuela
item.description: Financial firms are planning trips to Venezuela to scout out new investment opportunities. Bill Ackman praised the move as "good for America."
